subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which best describes glycogen?
options: A storage polysaccharide of glucose found in the liver and muscles
questions.explain: Glycogen is the body's storage carbohydrate, a branched polymer of glucose units.

questions.q: Which is the basic structural unit of a triglyceride?
options: One glucose and three fatty acids
Three amino acids and one glycerol
Three glycerols and one fatty acid
One glycerol and three fatty acids
questions.explain: A triglyceride consists of one glycerol molecule esterified with three fatty acids.

questions.q: Combining beans on toast to obtain a full set of essential amino acids is an example of:
questions.explain: Protein complementation combines two LBV foods whose limiting amino acids differ to give the full set.

questions.q: Osteoporosis is most directly linked to a long-term deficiency of:
questions.explain: Inadequate calcium and vitamin D reduce bone mineral density, leading to brittle bones.

questions.q: A food described as containing high biological value (HBV) protein is one that:
options: Contains all the essential amino acids
Contains no amino acids at all
questions.explain: HBV proteins supply all the indispensable (essential) amino acids the body cannot synthesise.

questions.q: Lecithin in egg yolk acts as an emulsifier in mayonnaise because it:
options: Has one part attracted to oil and one part attracted to water
Thickens the mixture by absorbing water
Coagulates the oil into solid particles
Raises the pH of the mixture
questions.explain: An emulsifier has hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends, holding oil and water together as a stable emulsion.

questions.q: Which is an example of an ethical factor influencing food choice?
options: Choosing free-range eggs on animal-welfare grounds
Selecting a familiar brand by habit
Choosing food because it is cheapest
questions.explain: Ethical choices, such as welfare-friendly or fair-trade products, are based on moral concerns.

questions.q: Vacuum packing helps preserve food chiefly by:
options: Heating the food to sterilise it
Removing oxygen so aerobic spoilage organisms cannot grow
Adding sugar to lower water activity
questions.explain: Removing oxygen inhibits aerobic micro-organisms and slows oxidative spoilage of the food.

questions.q: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is defined as the energy needed to:
options: Maintain essential body functions at complete rest
questions.explain: BMR is the energy required to sustain basic functions such as respiration and circulation at rest.

questions.q: A diet persistently high in saturated fat and salt most strongly increases the risk of:
questions.explain: High saturated fat and salt raise blood cholesterol and pressure, key risk factors for CHD.

questions.q: Water activity (aw) below approximately which value generally inhibits microbial growth?
questions.explain: Most micro-organisms cannot grow when water activity falls below about 0.6, the basis of drying.

questions.q: Bacterial spores, such as those of Clostridium and Bacillus, are a hazard because they:
options: Can survive normal cooking temperatures and germinate later
questions.explain: Heat-resistant spores can survive cooking and germinate into active bacteria if food is mishandled.

questions.q: In UK Dietary Reference Values, the Reference Nutrient Intake (RNI) is the amount of a nutrient that is:
options: The minimum needed by the few with lowest needs
An average for the whole population
Enough for almost all (about 97.5%) of the population group
questions.explain: The RNI meets the needs of about 97.5% of people in a group, so most will be adequately supplied.

questions.q: Which provides the most kilojoules of energy per gram?
questions.explain: Fat provides about 37 kJ per gram, more than double that of carbohydrate or protein.

questions.q: Buying locally produced, seasonal food can support sustainability mainly by:
options: Increasing the use of imported produce
Reducing food miles and associated transport emissions
Removing the need for any farming
questions.explain: Local seasonal food typically travels shorter distances, lowering transport emissions and supporting local producers.

questions.q: Pickling preserves food by:
options: Lowering the pH with acid such as vinegar
questions.explain: The acetic acid in vinegar lowers the pH below the range in which most spoilage bacteria grow.

questions.q: Which raising agent works by producing carbon dioxide when it reacts with an acid and moisture?
questions.explain: Baking powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid that release CO2 to aerate mixtures.

questions.q: In HACCP, a 'critical control point' is a step at which:
options: Control is essential to prevent or eliminate a hazard
questions.explain: A critical control point is a stage where control is essential to remove or reduce a hazard to a safe level.

questions.q: A kosher diet, following Jewish dietary law, prohibits:
options: Mixing meat and dairy in the same meal
questions.explain: Kosher rules forbid combining meat and dairy and prohibit certain foods such as pork and shellfish.

questions.q: Adding lemon juice to cut fruit slows enzymic browning because:
options: The acidity inhibits the enzyme activity
questions.explain: The low pH of lemon juice denatures the browning enzymes, slowing the reaction.

questions.q: E. coli O157 is a particularly dangerous pathogen because it:
options: Is destroyed instantly at fridge temperatures
Produces a toxin that can cause severe illness and kidney damage from a low dose
questions.explain: E. coli O157 needs only a small infective dose and can cause serious illness including kidney failure.

questions.q: Gelatinisation occurs when:
options: Fat and water are mixed with an emulsifier
Sugar is heated until it browns
Starch granules absorb liquid and swell on heating, thickening the mixture
Amino acids react with reducing sugars
questions.explain: On heating in liquid, starch granules absorb water, swell and burst, thickening the sauce.

questions.q: Clostridium perfringens is often linked to food poisoning from:
options: Large quantities of meat or stews left to cool slowly
questions.explain: C. perfringens spores survive cooking and multiply when bulk-cooked meat dishes cool too slowly.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of HACCP in a food business?
options: To set the retail price of food
To advertise the product to consumers
To identify and control critical points where hazards may occur
questions.explain: HACCP systematically identifies hazards and the critical control points where they must be controlled.

questions.q: A complete protein from a single plant source that supplies all essential amino acids is:
questions.explain: Soya is unusual among plant foods in supplying all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Listeria monocytogenes is of special concern because, unlike most pathogens, it can:
questions.explain: Listeria can multiply slowly at fridge temperatures, posing a risk in chilled ready-to-eat foods.

questions.q: By UK law, which information must legally appear on most pre-packed food labels?
options: A list of ingredients in descending order of weight
questions.explain: Ingredients must be listed by descending weight, alongside allergens, durability dates and other required details.

questions.q: Type-2 diabetes is characterised by:
options: Complete absence of insulin from birth
The body's cells becoming resistant to insulin
questions.explain: In type-2 diabetes cells become resistant to insulin, so blood glucose is poorly controlled.

questions.q: Mould growth on cheese such as blue cheese is an example of:
options: A harmful pathogen always causing illness
questions.explain: Certain moulds are cultivated deliberately to ripen and flavour foods like blue cheese.

questions.q: The Maillard reaction responsible for the brown crust on roast meat is a reaction between:
questions.explain: The Maillard reaction is non-enzymic browning between amino acids and reducing sugars on heating.
